capability.summary: Convert one floating-point magnitude between compatible Pint units
capability.description: Creates a default Pint UnitRegistry, multiplies a parsed float by the supplied source unit, converts it to the target unit, and returns the original numeric value, converted magnitude, and normalized target-unit string.
capability.problem_space: Scalar physical-unit conversion using Pint's default unit definitions and dimensional compatibility rules.

constraint.io_signature: Inputs: float-like value string, source-unit expression, and target-unit expression; output: JSON with original float, converted magnitude, and normalized unit text.
accepted_inputs: a string accepted by Python float for the scalar magnitude
source and target unit expressions recognized by a default Pint UnitRegistry and dimensionally convertible
constraint.output_shape: Success is an object with status="success", tool="lib.pint_convert", value as the parsed input float, result as the converted scalar magnitude, and unit as Pint's normalized target-unit string. A caught float-parse, unit-definition, dimensionality, offset-unit, or conversion exception produces an object with status="error", tool="lib.pint_convert", and message as the exception string, then exits with code 1.
limitations: accepts only a single Python float magnitude, not arrays, measurements with uncertainty, or a combined quantity expression
uses a fresh default UnitRegistry with no custom definitions, enabled contexts, or caller configuration
constructs quantities by multiplying magnitude and unit, which can reject offset units such as absolute temperatures under default Pint rules
does not preserve arbitrary decimal precision because the input is coerced to binary floating point
unknown units, incompatible dimensions, invalid floats, and conversion errors use the wrapper's error envelope

output_contract.description: Original float plus the converted scalar magnitude and Pint-normalized target unit.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: convert a scalar between compatible units
normalize a Pint unit conversion result
negative_intents: use custom Pint unit definitions or contexts
